subject: Science
title: Classifying insects, birds, mammals and reptiles

mcq.q: Which term best matches this description: an animal in a group whose adults have six legs and three main body regions?
mcq.method: Adult ants and butterflies have six legs attached to the thorax. Wings alone are unreliable because not all insects have them and birds also have wings.

mcq.q: Which term best matches this description: an animal belonging to the group characterised by feathers?
mcq.method: Feathers identify the group. Flight is not essential: hens and ostriches are birds even though their flight abilities differ.

mcq.q: Which term best matches this description: an animal in a group with hair at some life stage and milk production by females for their young?
mcq.method: Hair and feeding young with milk support classification as a mammal. Movement alone does not determine the group.

mcq.q: Which term best matches this description: an animal in a group generally characterised by dry scaly skin and breathing through lungs?
mcq.method: Snakes and lizards share these features. Snakes lack legs, so legs cannot be required for the group; fish scales also show why multiple features matter.

mcq.q: Which term best matches this description: the middle of the three main body regions of an insect, carrying its legs?
mcq.method: The thorax lies between the head and abdomen. Legs and, when present, wings attach there.

mcq.q: Which term best matches this description: paired sensory structures on an insect’s head?
mcq.method: These structures detect environmental information such as touch and chemicals. They are not extra walking legs.

mcq.q: Which term best matches this description: the distinctive body covering of birds, helping insulation and in many birds flight?
mcq.method: Both have feathers despite different habits. Covering is useful classification evidence whereas habitat alone is not.

mcq.q: Which term best matches this description: a characteristic mammalian covering that may be dense or sparse?
mcq.method: Goats have hair and females feed young with milk. Using more than one feature makes the classification stronger.

mcq.q: Which term best matches this description: an internal supporting structure shared by vertebrates?
mcq.method: Birds, mammals and reptiles have backbones. Insects have an external supporting covering and no backbone.

mcq.q: Which term best matches this description: grouping organisms according to shared features?
mcq.method: Good grouping uses consistent evidence about shared features. Colour, fear or whether an animal is liked is less useful for these biological groups.

mcq.method: Adult ants and butterflies have six legs attached to the thorax. Wings alone are unreliable because not all insects have them and birds also have wings.

mcq.method: Goats have hair and females feed young with milk. Using more than one feature makes the classification stronger.

mcq.method: Birds, mammals and reptiles have backbones. Insects have an external supporting covering and no backbone.

mcq.method: Good grouping uses consistent evidence about shared features. Colour, fear or whether an animal is liked is less useful for these biological groups.

subject: Science
title: Animal life processes: movement, nutrition and reproduction

mcq.q: Which term best matches this description: a change in the position of a whole organism or one of its body parts?
mcq.method: Movement can involve just one body part. Turning a head is movement even if the animal stays in the same place.

mcq.q: Which term best matches this description: movement of an organism from one place to another?
mcq.method: The entire animal changes location. Movement of a wing without changing place would not by itself be locomotion.

mcq.q: Which term best matches this description: obtaining and using food materials needed for life?
mcq.method: Food supplies materials for growth and repair and energy for activities. Eating is part of nutrition, not the only event in it.

mcq.q: Which term best matches this description: an animal whose diet consists mainly of plant material?
mcq.method: The diet, rather than the animal’s size, supports the classification. Grass is plant material that provides nutrients.

mcq.q: Which term best matches this description: an animal whose diet consists mainly of other animals?
mcq.method: The main food source is other animals. Classifying diet is different from judging whether the animal is dangerous.

mcq.q: Which term best matches this description: an animal that normally eats both plant and animal material?
mcq.method: Grains are plant material and insects are animal material. Both are represented in the diet.

mcq.q: Which term best matches this description: the biological process by which organisms produce new individuals?
mcq.method: New individuals continue the group over generations. Not every individual must reproduce to be alive.

mcq.q: Which term best matches this description: the young produced by a parent or parents?
mcq.method: A kid is a young goat. It resembles its parents in many features but need not look identical in every detail.

mcq.q: Which term best matches this description: a reproductive pattern in which young develop in eggs laid outside the parent’s body?
mcq.method: A developing chick can hatch from a fertilised egg under suitable conditions. Not every egg contains a developing chick.

mcq.q: Which term best matches this description: a reproductive pattern in which developed young emerge alive from the mother?
mcq.method: Goats normally give birth to live young and feed them milk. Different animal groups have different reproductive patterns.

mcq.method: New individuals continue the group over generations. Not every individual must reproduce to be alive.

mcq.q: A hen lays eggs from which chicks may hatch. Which reproductive pattern is shown?
mcq.method: A developing chick can hatch from a fertilised egg under suitable conditions. Not every egg contains a developing chick.

mcq.method: Goats normally give birth to live young and feed them milk. Different animal groups have different reproductive patterns.

title: Plant forms: trees, shrubs, climbers and creepers

mcq.q: Which term best matches this description: a woody plant usually having one main trunk and branches above the ground?
mcq.method: A main woody trunk supports the crown. Height alone is not enough because young trees can be short.

mcq.q: Which term best matches this description: a woody plant commonly having several stems branching near the ground?
mcq.method: Several low branches and woody stems support this classification. A shrub need not have the single main trunk typical of a tree.

mcq.q: Which term best matches this description: a plant with a stem that uses external support to grow upward?
mcq.method: The stem uses the stake for support rather than holding itself fully upright. Twining or tendrils may help attachment.

mcq.q: Which term best matches this description: a plant whose weak stems spread mainly along the ground?
mcq.method: Its stems spread horizontally and do not support a tall upright body. The growth habit, not the fruit’s size, decides the form.

mcq.q: Which term best matches this description: a plant with relatively soft, non-woody stems?
mcq.method: The stem texture is the key feature. The everyday meaning of a cooking herb is narrower than this botanical description.

mcq.q: Which term best matches this description: the main woody stem of a typical tree?
mcq.method: The trunk holds branches above the ground and contains pathways for transport. Roots have a different anchoring and absorbing role.

mcq.q: Which term best matches this description: a slender plant structure that can coil around a support?
mcq.method: Coiling helps attachment and support. The structure is not a root absorbing water from soil.

mcq.q: Which term best matches this description: a relatively hard, persistent stem containing wood?
mcq.method: Wood contributes support and persistence. Both trees and shrubs can have woody stems despite different branching patterns.

mcq.q: Which term best matches this description: a structure that holds a climbing stem in a useful position?
mcq.method: The trellis provides mechanical support. It does not replace water, light or mineral nutrients needed by the plant.

mcq.q: Which term best matches this description: the characteristic way a plant’s stems grow and are arranged?
mcq.method: Growth habit combines stem arrangement and support. Plant identification is stronger when observations are recorded before assigning labels.

subject: Science
title: Comparing the physical features of animal groups

mcq.q: Which term best matches this description: an animal in a group including frogs, often with moist skin and a life cycle linked to water?
mcq.method: Many frogs change from aquatic larvae to adults that can spend time on land. The pattern differs from a lizard’s dry scaly covering.

mcq.q: Which term best matches this description: a usually damp body covering characteristic of many amphibians?
mcq.method: A frog’s skin must be protected from drying and damage. A lizard typically has a drier, scaly covering.

mcq.q: Which term best matches this description: a protective covering typical of reptiles such as lizards?
mcq.method: Dry scales are useful reptile evidence when combined with other features. Scales alone do not separate reptiles from every other animal group.

mcq.q: Which term best matches this description: the usual number of legs on an adult insect?
mcq.method: Adult insects have three pairs of legs. Spiders have four pairs and are not insects, even though both groups include small crawling animals.

mcq.q: Which term best matches this description: the insect arrangement of head, thorax and abdomen?
mcq.method: Head, thorax and abdomen have different roles. Legs attach to the thorax, so labels should reflect the actual arrangement.

mcq.q: Which term best matches this description: structures in female mammals that produce milk for their young?
mcq.method: Milk provides nourishment for the young. Together with hair, this supports mammalian classification more reliably than walking on four legs alone.

mcq.q: Which term best matches this description: a distinctive body covering identifying birds?
mcq.method: The pigeon has feathers; the bat has hair and feeds its young milk. Shared flight does not mean the same animal group.

mcq.q: Which term best matches this description: an animal possessing a backbone?
mcq.method: They have internal skeletons with backbones despite their different coverings. A butterfly lacks a backbone.

mcq.q: Which term best matches this description: an external supporting and protective covering?
mcq.method: The covering supports and protects from outside. A vertebrate’s main supporting skeleton is internal.

mcq.q: Which term best matches this description: a sequence of feature-based choices used to identify an organism?
mcq.method: Each choice should use observable, clear features. An ambiguous question such as “is it nice?” is not a sound scientific distinction.

mcq.method: A frog’s skin must be protected from drying and damage. A lizard typically has a drier, scaly covering.

mcq.q: A mother goat feeds her kid with milk produced by which structures?
mcq.method: Milk provides nourishment for the young. Together with hair, this supports mammalian classification more reliably than walking on four legs alone.

mcq.method: The pigeon has feathers; the bat has hair and feeds its young milk. Shared flight does not mean the same animal group.

mcq.q: A goat, lizard and frog all have which general classification?
mcq.method: They have internal skeletons with backbones despite their different coverings. A butterfly lacks a backbone.

mcq.q: An insect’s firm outer covering is an example of what?
mcq.method: The covering supports and protects from outside. A vertebrate’s main supporting skeleton is internal.

mcq.method: Each choice should use observable, clear features. An ambiguous question such as “is it nice?” is not a sound scientific distinction.

essays.q: Which covering is commonly observed on a frog rather than a lizard?
essays.answer: Moist skin

essays.q: Explain why touching or drying a frog’s skin can be harmful.
essays.answer: A frog’s skin must be protected from drying and damage. A lizard typically has a drier, scaly covering.

essays.q: Explain the term “Dry scales”.
essays.answer: A protective covering typical of reptiles such as lizards

essays.q: Which covering helps identify a lizard among the pictured animals?
essays.answer: Dry scales

essays.q: Explain why more than one feature should be used in classification.
essays.answer: Dry scales are useful reptile evidence when combined with other features. Scales alone do not separate reptiles from every other animal group.

essays.q: Explain the term “Six legs”.
essays.answer: The usual number of legs on an adult insect

essays.q: Which feature distinguishes an adult butterfly from a spider?
essays.answer: Six legs

essays.q: Explain why a spider should not be placed in the insect group.
essays.answer: Adult insects have three pairs of legs. Spiders have four pairs and are not insects, even though both groups include small crawling animals.

essays.q: Explain the term “Three body regions”.
essays.answer: The insect arrangement of head, thorax and abdomen

essays.q: An ant drawing should show which main body arrangement?
essays.answer: Three body regions

essays.q: Name the three regions and state where the legs attach.
essays.answer: Head, thorax and abdomen have different roles. Legs attach to the thorax, so labels should reflect the actual arrangement.

essays.q: Explain the term “Mammary glands”.
essays.answer: Structures in female mammals that produce milk for their young

essays.q: A mother goat feeds her kid with milk produced by which structures?
essays.answer: Mammary glands

essays.q: Explain why milk production is useful evidence for classifying a goat.
essays.answer: Milk provides nourishment for the young. Together with hair, this supports mammalian classification more reliably than walking on four legs alone.

essays.q: Explain the term “Feathers”.
essays.answer: A distinctive body covering identifying birds

essays.q: A bat and a pigeon both fly. Which covering identifies the pigeon as a bird?
essays.answer: Feathers

essays.q: Explain why flight alone cannot separate birds from mammals.
essays.answer: The pigeon has feathers; the bat has hair and feeds its young milk. Shared flight does not mean the same animal group.

essays.q: Explain the term “Vertebrate”.
essays.answer: An animal possessing a backbone

essays.q: A goat, lizard and frog all have which general classification?
essays.answer: Vertebrate

essays.q: Explain a shared feature of these animals and contrast it with an insect.
essays.answer: They have internal skeletons with backbones despite their different coverings. A butterfly lacks a backbone.

essays.q: Explain the term “Exoskeleton”.
essays.answer: An external supporting and protective covering

essays.q: An insect’s firm outer covering is an example of what?
essays.answer: Exoskeleton

essays.q: Compare external and internal support using an insect and a goat.
essays.answer: The covering supports and protects from outside. A vertebrate’s main supporting skeleton is internal.

essays.q: Explain the term “Classification key”.
essays.answer: A sequence of feature-based choices used to identify an organism

essays.q: A chart asks “feathers present?” and then offers further choices. What kind of identification tool is it?
essays.answer: Classification key

essays.q: Write one useful yes/no feature question for identifying an animal group.
essays.answer: Each choice should use observable, clear features. An ambiguous question such as “is it nice?” is not a sound scientific distinction.

mcq.q: Which term best matches this description: two or more substances physically combined?
mcq.method: The substances remain present even when stirred. Putting materials together does not necessarily form a new chemical substance.

mcq.q: Which term best matches this description: liquids that do not form one uniform liquid phase when combined?
mcq.method: The liquids remain in separate phases. Shaking can make small droplets temporarily but does not permanently make them mix uniformly.

mcq.q: Which term best matches this description: liquids that mix uniformly under the stated conditions?
mcq.method: The pair mixes at the liquid level rather than separating into layers. A uniform appearance alone does not show that only one substance is present.

mcq.q: Which term best matches this description: a distinct region of one liquid above or below another?
mcq.method: Distinct regions make the boundary visible and can support separation. The location depends partly on density, not simply on colour.

mcq.q: Which term best matches this description: mass per unit volume of a substance?
mcq.method: Cooking oil usually has lower density than water and forms the upper layer. Density is not the same as the total mass of a large container.

mcq.q: Which term best matches this description: the period allowed for a disturbed mixture to separate or become less turbulent?
mcq.method: Small droplets can combine into clearer layers while the mixture stands. Repeated shaking delays the observation of a stable boundary.

mcq.q: Which term best matches this description: carefully pouring off one separated liquid region without greatly disturbing the rest?
mcq.method: Careful pouring can remove part of a layer but may mix some liquid at the boundary. It is not always a complete separation.

mcq.q: Which term best matches this description: an apparatus with a tap used to separate suitable immiscible liquid layers?
mcq.method: The lower layer leaves first, and the tap is closed near the boundary. The apparatus is unsuitable for separating two fully miscible liquids by this method.

mcq.q: Which term best matches this description: a comparison keeping relevant conditions the same except the chosen variable?
mcq.method: Keeping volume, containers and waiting time similar helps relate the difference to stirring rather than another changed condition.

essays.answer: The substances remain present even when stirred. Putting materials together does not necessarily form a new chemical substance.

mcq.method: Returning to a starting state allows repetition to be recognised. Different cycles may take very different times.

mcq.q: Which term best matches this description: turning around an axis?
mcq.method: The object turns about an axis rather than travelling along a straight line. One full turn returns its orientation to the start.

mcq.q: Which term best matches this description: repeated movement to and fro about a central position?
mcq.method: The movement alternates around a central position. One full oscillation includes the return to the same side in the same direction of motion.

mcq.q: Which term best matches this description: the time taken for one complete cycle?
mcq.method: The measurement is a time interval. Measuring several turns and dividing by their number can reduce the effect of timing errors.

mcq.method: The hand revisits positions at regular intervals. Different hands complete their cycles at different rates.

mcq.method: The axis identifies the line of turning. It should not be confused with a path around another object.

mcq.q: Which term best matches this description: a path followed by an object as it moves around another under gravity?
mcq.method: Orbiting is movement around another body. Rotation is spinning around the object’s own axis, so the two motions differ.

mcq.q: Which term best matches this description: earth’s natural satellite, seen mainly because it reflects sunlight?

mcq.q: Which term best matches this description: a very distant luminous object that produces its own light?
mcq.method: Stars appear small mainly because they are far away. The Sun is a star but appears much larger because it is much nearer.

mcq.q: Which term best matches this description: a visible collection of tiny water droplets or ice crystals in the atmosphere?
mcq.method: Clouds belong to Earth’s atmosphere and can move with the air. They are not solid objects in outer space.

mcq.q: Which term best matches this description: a body orbiting a star and seen by reflected light rather than producing starlight?

essays.q: Explain why leaves are often positioned where they can receive light.
essays.answer: Many leaves receive light and exchange gases. Green tissues use light energy to make sugars from water and carbon dioxide.

essays.q: Explain the term “Flower”.
essays.answer: A reproductive structure of a flowering plant

essays.q: Which part may produce pollen and later give rise to seeds after reproductive processes?
essays.answer: Flower

essays.q: Explain why a flower is more than a colourful decoration.
essays.answer: Flowers support reproduction, not just decoration. After pollination and fertilisation, seeds may develop and parts of the flower may form fruit.

essays.q: Explain the term “Fruit”.
essays.answer: A structure commonly developing from a flower’s ovary and containing or protecting seeds

essays.q: A mango surrounds a seed with fleshy tissue. Which structure is the mango as a whole?
essays.answer: Fruit

essays.q: State two ways a fruit can help the next generation of plants.
essays.answer: Fruits protect seeds and can help dispersal. Not all fruits are sweet or eaten by people.

essays.q: Explain the term “Seed”.
essays.answer: A structure containing a young plant and resources or tissues supporting its early development

essays.q: What can grow into a new plant when suitable germination conditions are present?
essays.answer: Seed

essays.q: Explain why not every seed necessarily germinates.
essays.answer: A viable seed contains a living embryo. Water, oxygen and suitable temperature support germination, but a damaged or dead seed may not grow.

essays.q: Explain the term “Seed coat”.
essays.answer: The outer protective covering of a seed

essays.q: Which part protects the young plant inside a bean seed?
essays.answer: Seed coat

essays.q: Explain why a protective covering must still permit germination under suitable conditions.
essays.answer: The covering provides protection. Water uptake and growth lead to changes that allow the emerging root to break through it.

essays.q: Explain the term “Photosynthesis”.
essays.answer: The process in which green tissues use light to make sugars from water and carbon dioxide

essays.q: A green leaf uses sunlight to make food. Which process is this?
essays.answer: Photosynthesis

essays.q: Distinguish the source of energy from the materials used to make plant food.
essays.answer: Light supplies energy; water and carbon dioxide supply materials. The plant is not eating soil in the way an animal eats food.

essays.q: Explain the term “Pollination”.
essays.answer: Transfer of pollen to a flower’s stigma

essays.q: An insect carries pollen from one flower to a suitable stigma. Which process occurs?
essays.answer: Pollination

essays.q: Explain why pollination and seed germination are different processes.
essays.answer: Pollen transfer is part of reproduction. It is not identical to fertilisation, which is a later biological event when successful reproduction proceeds.

essays.q: Explain the term “Transport”.
essays.answer: Movement of water and other materials between plant parts

essays.q: Water taken up by roots reaches leaves through internal pathways. Which function is shown?
essays.answer: Transport

essays.q: Explain why harm to a stem can affect leaves above it.
essays.answer: Materials move between organs that perform different jobs. Damage to important transport pathways can affect distant parts of a plant.

mcq.q: Which term best matches this description: the young root that commonly emerges first during germination?

mcq.q: Which term best matches this description: the young shoot of the embryo?

essays.q: Explain the term “Germination”.
essays.answer: The beginning of growth of a seed’s embryo under suitable conditions

essays.q: A bean seed swells, splits its coat and produces a young root. What process is beginning?
essays.answer: Germination

essays.q: Distinguish germination from the earlier production of a seed.
essays.answer: A viable embryo resumes growth. This is different from producing the seed inside a flower and fruit.

essays.q: Explain the term “Embryo”.
essays.answer: The young plant inside a seed

essays.q: Which living structure develops into the seedling?
essays.answer: Embryo

essays.q: Explain why a glass bead cannot germinate even if it receives water.
essays.answer: The embryo contains the beginnings of root and shoot. A viable embryo, not simply a seed-shaped object, is needed for growth.

essays.answer: The protective outer covering of a seed

essays.q: Explain why early root growth helps a new seedling.
essays.answer: The emerging root helps establish absorption and anchorage. Its function differs from the shoot that later carries leaves.

essays.q: Explain the term “Plumule”.
essays.answer: The young shoot of the embryo

essays.q: Which developing structure grows upward and gives rise to shoot tissues and leaves?
essays.answer: Plumule

essays.q: Compare the main roles of the young root and young shoot.
essays.answer: The shoot supports future leaves and access to light. Roots and shoots develop different structures suited to different jobs.

essays.q: Explain the term “Cotyledon”.
essays.answer: A seed leaf that may store food or help transfer stored food to the embryo

essays.q: The fleshy seed leaves of a bean supply food during early growth. What are they called?
essays.answer: Cotyledon

essays.q: Explain why a germinating seed can begin growing before it has large green leaves.
essays.answer: Stored food supports growth before the seedling makes enough food by photosynthesis. Cotyledon roles vary among different seeds.

essays.q: Explain the term “Moisture”.
essays.answer: Water available to the seed without completely excluding air

essays.q: Moist paper supports germination better than dry paper for otherwise similar viable beans. Which need is supplied?
essays.answer: Moisture

essays.q: Explain why both dryness and excessive water can prevent healthy germination.
essays.answer: Water uptake activates growth processes. Excess water can exclude oxygen, so damp conditions are not the same as submerging every seed.

essays.q: Explain the term “Oxygen”.
essays.answer: A gas needed for respiration by a germinating seed

essays.q: Which gas must be available so a germinating seed can release energy from stored food?
essays.answer: Oxygen

essays.q: Explain why a seed needs air as well as water.
essays.answer: Respiration supplies energy for growth. Waterlogged conditions may reduce gas availability even when plenty of water is present.

essays.q: Explain the term “Suitable temperature”.
essays.answer: A range of warmth allowing germination processes to proceed normally

essays.q: Two moist seeds grow differently in very cold and moderately warm conditions. Which environmental factor differs?
essays.answer: Suitable temperature

essays.q: Explain why “the hotter the better” is not a sound germination rule.
essays.answer: Growth processes depend on temperature; extremely hot or cold conditions may prevent germination. The suitable range depends on the species.

essays.q: Explain the term “Control”.
essays.answer: A comparison setup used to help test the role of one factor

essays.q: Dry paper is compared with moist paper while seed type and warmth are kept the same. What is the dry setup’s role?
essays.answer: Control

essays.q: Explain why the same seed type and several seeds should be used in both setups.
essays.answer: The comparison helps isolate the effect of moisture. Several seeds in each condition reduce the risk of drawing conclusions from one unusual seed.

subject: Science

mcq.q: An adult animal has six legs, antennae, a head, thorax and abdomen. Which group fits it?
mcq.method: Adult ants and butterflies have six legs attached to the thorax. Wings alone are unreliable because not all insects have them and birds also have wings.

mcq.q: A cow feeds mainly on grass. Which dietary group fits it?
mcq.method: The diet, rather than the animal’s size, supports the classification. Grass is plant material that provides nutrients.

mcq.q: A climbing plant grips a thin support with a curling structure. What is it called?
mcq.method: Coiling helps attachment and support. The structure is not a root absorbing water from soil.

mcq.q: A chart asks “feathers present?” and then offers further choices. What kind of identification tool is it?
mcq.method: Each choice should use observable, clear features. An ambiguous question such as “is it nice?” is not a sound scientific distinction.

mcq.q: A polished spoon feels even compared with coarse sandpaper. Which property describes the spoon’s surface?
mcq.method: Texture describes the surface rather than the entire object’s shape. Safe touching can compare texture without scratching or damaging samples.

mcq.q: A class leaves stirred oil and water untouched before observing the boundary. What are they allowing?
mcq.method: Small droplets can combine into clearer layers while the mixture stands. Repeated shaking delays the observation of a stable boundary.

mcq.q: A hen, goat and lizard share which structure that an insect lacks?
mcq.method: Birds, mammals and reptiles have backbones. Insects have an external supporting covering and no backbone.

mcq.q: A hen walks from its coop to a water bowl. What kind of movement is this?
mcq.method: The entire animal changes location. Movement of a wing without changing place would not by itself be locomotion.

mcq.q: A small plant has soft green stems rather than persistent woody branches. Which description fits?
mcq.method: The stem texture is the key feature. The everyday meaning of a cooking herb is narrower than this botanical description.

mcq.q: A goat, lizard and frog all have which general classification?
mcq.method: They have internal skeletons with backbones despite their different coverings. A butterfly lacks a backbone.

mcq.q: A wooden block is harder to dent with gentle pressure than a sponge. Which property is compared?
mcq.method: Hardness concerns resistance to local deformation. A hard material may still fracture under impact; glass provides a familiar example.

mcq.q: After standing, oil occupies a separate upper region in water. What is this region called?
mcq.method: Distinct regions make the boundary visible and can support separation. The location depends partly on density, not simply on colour.

mcq.q: A duck and a hen share which distinctive body covering?
mcq.method: Both have feathers despite different habits. Covering is useful classification evidence whereas habitat alone is not.

mcq.q: A goat gives birth to a kid rather than laying an egg. Which pattern is shown?
mcq.method: Goats normally give birth to live young and feed them milk. Different animal groups have different reproductive patterns.

mcq.q: A bean vine grows upward around a stake. Which form is shown?
mcq.method: The stem uses the stake for support rather than holding itself fully upright. Twining or tendrils may help attachment.

essays.q: Explain the meaning of “Mammal”, including a supporting scientific point.
essays.answer: An animal in a group with hair at some life stage and milk production by females for their young. Hair and feeding young with milk support classification as a mammal. Movement alone does not determine the group.

essays.q: An ant touches objects with two slender structures on its head. What are these? Give a scientific reason for your answer.
essays.answer: Antennae. These structures detect environmental information such as touch and chemicals. They are not extra walking legs.

essays.q: Explain how this structure separates an insect from a bird without referring to wings.
essays.answer: Birds, mammals and reptiles have backbones. Insects have an external supporting covering and no backbone.

essays.q: Explain the meaning of “Omnivore”, including a supporting scientific point.
essays.answer: An animal that normally eats both plant and animal material. Grains are plant material and insects are animal material. Both are represented in the diet.

essays.q: A hen lays eggs from which chicks may hatch. Which reproductive pattern is shown? Give a scientific reason for your answer.
essays.answer: Egg-laying. A developing chick can hatch from a fertilised egg under suitable conditions. Not every egg contains a developing chick.

essays.q: Distinguish moving a body part from changing the location of the whole animal.
essays.answer: The entire animal changes location. Movement of a wing without changing place would not by itself be locomotion.

essays.q: Explain the meaning of “Support”, including a supporting scientific point.
essays.answer: A structure that holds a climbing stem in a useful position. The trellis provides mechanical support. It does not replace water, light or mineral nutrients needed by the plant.

essays.q: A hibiscus bush has several woody stems from close to the soil. Which form best fits it? Give a scientific reason for your answer.
essays.answer: Shrub. Several low branches and woody stems support this classification. A shrub need not have the single main trunk typical of a tree.

essays.q: Explain why stem structure is more useful than culinary use for this classification.
essays.answer: The stem texture is the key feature. The everyday meaning of a cooking herb is narrower than this botanical description.

essays.q: Explain the meaning of “Moist skin”, including a supporting scientific point.
essays.answer: A usually damp body covering characteristic of many amphibians. A frog’s skin must be protected from drying and damage. A lizard typically has a drier, scaly covering.

essays.q: An ant drawing should show which main body arrangement? Give a scientific reason for your answer.
essays.answer: Three body regions. Head, thorax and abdomen have different roles. Legs attach to the thorax, so labels should reflect the actual arrangement.

essays.q: Explain a shared feature of these animals and contrast it with an insect.
essays.answer: They have internal skeletons with backbones despite their different coverings. A butterfly lacks a backbone.

essays.q: Explain the meaning of “Transparent”, including a supporting scientific point.
essays.answer: Allowing enough light through for objects to be seen clearly. Light passes through so the image remains visible. Being colourless and being transparent are related observations but not the same definition.

essays.q: A cloth towel takes up spilled water. Which property is useful? Give a scientific reason for your answer.
essays.answer: Absorbent. Water enters spaces in the fibres. A waterproof surface instead resists water passing through it.

essays.q: Explain why a hard material is not necessarily unbreakable.
essays.answer: Hardness concerns resistance to local deformation. A hard material may still fracture under impact; glass provides a familiar example.

essays.q: Explain the meaning of “Separating funnel”, including a supporting scientific point.
essays.answer: An apparatus with a tap used to separate suitable immiscible liquid layers. The lower layer leaves first, and the tap is closed near the boundary. The apparatus is unsuitable for separating two fully miscible liquids by this method.

essays.q: Water and cooking oil are put into the same container. What has been made? Give a scientific reason for your answer.
essays.answer: Mixture. The substances remain present even when stirred. Putting materials together does not necessarily form a new chemical substance.

essays.q: Explain why visible layers are useful when planning separation.
essays.answer: Distinct regions make the boundary visible and can support separation. The location depends partly on density, not simply on colour.

essays.q: Explain the meaning of “Insect”, including a supporting scientific point.
essays.answer: An animal in a group whose adults have six legs and three main body regions. Adult ants and butterflies have six legs attached to the thorax. Wings alone are unreliable because not all insects have them and birds also have wings.

essays.q: An animal has dry scales, breathes with lungs and crawls on land. Which target group best fits it? Give a scientific reason for your answer.
essays.answer: Reptile. Snakes and lizards share these features. Snakes lack legs, so legs cannot be required for the group; fish scales also show why multiple features matter.

essays.q: Explain how this covering supports grouping a hen and a duck together.
essays.answer: Both have feathers despite different habits. Covering is useful classification evidence whereas habitat alone is not.

essays.q: Explain the meaning of “Herbivore”, including a supporting scientific point.
essays.answer: An animal whose diet consists mainly of plant material. The diet, rather than the animal’s size, supports the classification. Grass is plant material that provides nutrients.

essays.q: An adult animal produces young of its own kind. Which life process is shown? Give a scientific reason for your answer.
essays.answer: Reproduction. New individuals continue the group over generations. Not every individual must reproduce to be alive.

essays.q: Compare the birth of a kid with the hatching of a chick.
essays.answer: Goats normally give birth to live young and feed them milk. Different animal groups have different reproductive patterns.

essays.q: Explain the meaning of “Tendril”, including a supporting scientific point.
essays.answer: A slender plant structure that can coil around a support. Coiling helps attachment and support. The structure is not a root absorbing water from soil.

essays.q: A class compares plants that stand upright, climb or spread on the ground. Which feature are they comparing? Give a scientific reason for your answer.
essays.answer: Growth habit. Growth habit combines stem arrangement and support. Plant identification is stronger when observations are recorded before assigning labels.

essays.q: Explain the role of the stake in the bean vine’s growth.
essays.answer: The stem uses the stake for support rather than holding itself fully upright. Twining or tendrils may help attachment.

essays.q: Explain the meaning of “Classification key”, including a supporting scientific point.
essays.answer: A sequence of feature-based choices used to identify an organism. Each choice should use observable, clear features. An ambiguous question such as “is it nice?” is not a sound scientific distinction.

essays.q: Which covering helps identify a lizard among the pictured animals? Give a scientific reason for your answer.
essays.answer: Dry scales. Dry scales are useful reptile evidence when combined with other features. Scales alone do not separate reptiles from every other animal group.

essays.q: Explain why milk production is useful evidence for classifying a goat.
essays.answer: Milk provides nourishment for the young. Together with hair, this supports mammalian classification more reliably than walking on four legs alone.

essays.q: Explain the meaning of “Smooth texture”, including a supporting scientific point.
essays.answer: A surface with relatively few noticeable bumps under gentle touch. Texture describes the surface rather than the entire object’s shape. Safe touching can compare texture without scratching or damaging samples.

essays.q: A cardboard cover hides the picture behind it. Which optical property is shown? Give a scientific reason for your answer.
essays.answer: Opaque. Blocking light protects privacy or shades an object. Thinness alone does not prove that a material will be transparent.

essays.q: Explain why a raincoat with a tear may leak despite waterproof fabric.
essays.answer: The coating or material resists water penetration. Seams and tears can still allow leaks, so the whole object must be checked.

essays.q: Explain the meaning of “Settling time”, including a supporting scientific point.
essays.answer: The period allowed for a disturbed mixture to separate or become less turbulent. Small droplets can combine into clearer layers while the mixture stands. Repeated shaking delays the observation of a stable boundary.

essays.q: A pupil writes “two layers formed after five minutes”. What kind of record is this? Give a scientific reason for your answer.
essays.answer: Observation. The statement records an event and a time rather than claiming an untested cause. Explanations should be based on such evidence.

essays.q: Explain why shaking does not permanently remove the two layers.
essays.answer: The liquids remain in separate phases. Shaking can make small droplets temporarily but does not permanently make them mix uniformly.

essays.q: Explain the meaning of “Backbone”, including a supporting scientific point.
essays.answer: An internal supporting structure shared by vertebrates. Birds, mammals and reptiles have backbones. Insects have an external supporting covering and no backbone.

essays.q: A hen cannot fly far but has feathers. In which group should it be classified? Give a scientific reason for your answer.
essays.answer: Bird. Feathers identify the group. Flight is not essential: hens and ostriches are birds even though their flight abilities differ.

essays.q: Describe the location of this region and state what attaches to it.
essays.answer: The thorax lies between the head and abdomen. Legs and, when present, wings attach there.

essays.q: Explain the meaning of “Locomotion”, including a supporting scientific point.
essays.answer: Movement of an organism from one place to another. The entire animal changes location. Movement of a wing without changing place would not by itself be locomotion.

essays.q: A lion eats mainly animal flesh. Which dietary group fits it? Give a scientific reason for your answer.
essays.answer: Carnivore. The main food source is other animals. Classifying diet is different from judging whether the animal is dangerous.

essays.q: Describe one similarity and one possible difference between an offspring and its parent.
essays.answer: A kid is a young goat. It resembles its parents in many features but need not look identical in every detail.

essays.q: Explain the meaning of “Herb”, including a supporting scientific point.
essays.answer: A plant with relatively soft, non-woody stems. The stem texture is the key feature. The everyday meaning of a cooking herb is narrower than this botanical description.

essays.q: Which stem type helps trees and shrubs support their branches over many seasons? Give a scientific reason for your answer.
essays.answer: Woody stem. Wood contributes support and persistence. Both trees and shrubs can have woody stems despite different branching patterns.

essays.q: Explain why a young mango plant can still be classified as a tree.
essays.answer: A main woody trunk supports the crown. Height alone is not enough because young trees can be short.

essays.q: Explain the meaning of “Thorax”, including a supporting scientific point.
essays.answer: The middle of the three main body regions of an insect, carrying its legs. The thorax lies between the head and abdomen. Legs and, when present, wings attach there.

essays.q: Which covering on a goat helps distinguish it from a hen? Give a scientific reason for your answer.
essays.answer: Hair. Goats have hair and females feed young with milk. Using more than one feature makes the classification stronger.

essays.q: Explain why legs and body regions are better evidence than wings alone when identifying an adult insect.
essays.answer: Adult ants and butterflies have six legs attached to the thorax. Wings alone are unreliable because not all insects have them and birds also have wings.

essays.q: Explain the meaning of “Offspring”, including a supporting scientific point.
essays.answer: The young produced by a parent or parents. A kid is a young goat. It resembles its parents in many features but need not look identical in every detail.

essays.q: A goat turns its head while standing in one place. Which life activity is shown? Give a scientific reason for your answer.
essays.answer: Movement. Movement can involve just one body part. Turning a head is movement even if the animal stays in the same place.

essays.q: Explain why the cow belongs to this dietary group.
essays.answer: The diet, rather than the animal’s size, supports the classification. Grass is plant material that provides nutrients.

essays.q: Explain the meaning of “Tree”, including a supporting scientific point.
essays.answer: A woody plant usually having one main trunk and branches above the ground. A main woody trunk supports the crown. Height alone is not enough because young trees can be short.

essays.q: A pumpkin plant spreads over the soil without climbing a support. Which form is shown? Give a scientific reason for your answer.
essays.answer: Creeper. Its stems spread horizontally and do not support a tall upright body. The growth habit, not the fruit’s size, decides the form.

essays.q: Explain how a tendril helps a climber reach upward.
essays.answer: Coiling helps attachment and support. The structure is not a root absorbing water from soil.

essays.q: Explain the meaning of “Six legs”, including a supporting scientific point.
essays.answer: The usual number of legs on an adult insect. Adult insects have three pairs of legs. Spiders have four pairs and are not insects, even though both groups include small crawling animals.

essays.q: A bat and a pigeon both fly. Which covering identifies the pigeon as a bird? Give a scientific reason for your answer.
essays.answer: Feathers. The pigeon has feathers; the bat has hair and feeds its young milk. Shared flight does not mean the same animal group.

essays.q: Write one useful yes/no feature question for identifying an animal group.
essays.answer: Each choice should use observable, clear features. An ambiguous question such as “is it nice?” is not a sound scientific distinction.

essays.q: Explain the meaning of “Flexible”, including a supporting scientific point.
essays.answer: Able to bend without readily breaking under suitable conditions. Flexibility concerns bending. A material can be flexible but not stretch very much, so flexibility and elasticity should not be confused.

essays.q: A learner chooses absorbent cloth for a towel instead of a plastic sheet. What process is being carried out? Give a scientific reason for your answer.
essays.answer: Material selection. The intended use determines which properties matter. No single material is best for every purpose.

essays.q: Distinguish surface texture from an object’s overall shape.
essays.answer: Texture describes the surface rather than the entire object’s shape. Safe touching can compare texture without scratching or damaging samples.

essays.q: Explain the meaning of “Fair comparison”, including a supporting scientific point.
essays.answer: A comparison keeping relevant conditions the same except the chosen variable. Keeping volume, containers and waiting time similar helps relate the difference to stirring rather than another changed condition.

essays.q: A teacher’s approved pair of liquids forms one uniform phase after mixing. Which term describes the pair? Give a scientific reason for your answer.
essays.answer: Miscible liquids. The pair mixes at the liquid level rather than separating into layers. A uniform appearance alone does not show that only one substance is present.

essays.q: Explain why observations immediately after shaking may differ from observations later.
essays.answer: Small droplets can combine into clearer layers while the mixture stands. Repeated shaking delays the observation of a stable boundary.

essays.q: Explain the meaning of “Oscillation”, including a supporting scientific point.
essays.answer: Repeated movement to and fro about a central position. The movement alternates around a central position. One full oscillation includes the return to the same side in the same direction of motion.

essays.q: What does a globe rotate around in a classroom model? Give a scientific reason for your answer.
essays.answer: Axis. The axis identifies the line of turning. It should not be confused with a path around another object.

essays.q: Explain how observing several cycles can support a testable prediction.
essays.answer: A repeated pattern supports an expectation that can be tested. A prediction should be checked rather than treated as certain regardless of evidence.

essays.q: Explain the meaning of “Atmosphere”, including a supporting scientific point.
essays.answer: The layer of gases surrounding Earth. Clouds form within the atmosphere, relatively close compared with the Moon or stars. This distinguishes weather phenomena from distant astronomical objects.

essays.q: Moonlight reaches our eyes mainly as which kind of light? Give a scientific reason for your answer.
essays.answer: Reflected light. Sunlight strikes the Moon and some is directed toward Earth. The Moon therefore acts differently from the Sun as a light source.

essays.q: Explain why the statement “the Moon is only in the night sky” is incorrect.
essays.answer: The Moon reflects sunlight and can be above the horizon in daylight. It is not restricted to appearing only at night.

essays.q: Explain the meaning of “Air movement”, including a supporting scientific point.
essays.answer: Movement of surrounding air that can carry water vapour away. Moving air removes moist air near the surface, helping more water evaporate. Temperature and humidity also affect drying.

essays.q: What form of water enters the air during evaporation? Give a scientific reason for your answer.
essays.answer: Water vapour. The gas is not normally seen directly. A visible mist consists mainly of tiny liquid droplets rather than the invisible gas itself.

essays.q: Explain why leaf openings matter for both gas exchange and water loss.
essays.answer: Openings permit gases to move between the leaf and air. Their regulation affects water loss as well as gas exchange.

essays.q: Explain the meaning of “Contamination”, including a supporting scientific point.
essays.answer: Introduction of harmful or unwanted substances into water. Microbes or dirt can enter a previously safe supply. Preventing contamination after treatment is as important as the treatment step.

essays.q: Which heat-based method can help disinfect microbiologically unsafe water when properly carried out by an adult? Give a scientific reason for your answer.
essays.answer: Boiling. Proper boiling addresses many microbes, but it does not reliably remove harmful dissolved chemicals. Cooling and storage must avoid recontamination.

essays.q: Explain how dipping a dirty cup can affect the entire stored supply.
essays.answer: Avoiding contact with the stored water reduces transfer of microbes. A clean serving cup still matters after dispensing.

essays.q: Explain the meaning of “Fruit”, including a supporting scientific point.
essays.answer: A structure commonly developing from a flower’s ovary and containing or protecting seeds. Fruits protect seeds and can help dispersal. Not all fruits are sweet or eaten by people.

essays.q: A green leaf uses sunlight to make food. Which process is this? Give a scientific reason for your answer.
essays.answer: Photosynthesis. Light supplies energy; water and carbon dioxide supply materials. The plant is not eating soil in the way an animal eats food.

essays.q: State two important functions of roots.
essays.answer: Roots hold the plant and absorb water and minerals. They do not normally absorb prepared sugary food directly from soil.

essays.q: Explain the meaning of “Oxygen”, including a supporting scientific point.
essays.answer: A gas needed for respiration by a germinating seed. Respiration supplies energy for growth. Waterlogged conditions may reduce gas availability even when plenty of water is present.

essays.q: A bean seed swells, splits its coat and produces a young root. What process is beginning? Give a scientific reason for your answer.
essays.answer: Germination. A viable embryo resumes growth. This is different from producing the seed inside a flower and fruit.

essays.q: Explain why early root growth helps a new seedling.
essays.answer: The emerging root helps establish absorption and anchorage. Its function differs from the shoot that later carries leaves.

essays.q: Explain the meaning of “Insect”, including a supporting scientific point.
essays.answer: An animal in a group whose adults have six legs and three main body regions. Adult ants and butterflies have six legs attached to the thorax. Wings alone are unreliable because not all insects have them and birds also have wings.

essays.q: An animal has dry scales, breathes with lungs and crawls on land. Which target group best fits it? Give a scientific reason for your answer.
essays.answer: Reptile. Snakes and lizards share these features. Snakes lack legs, so legs cannot be required for the group; fish scales also show why multiple features matter.

essays.q: Explain how this covering supports grouping a hen and a duck together.
essays.answer: Both have feathers despite different habits. Covering is useful classification evidence whereas habitat alone is not.

essays.q: Explain the meaning of “Herbivore”, including a supporting scientific point.
essays.answer: An animal whose diet consists mainly of plant material. The diet, rather than the animal’s size, supports the classification. Grass is plant material that provides nutrients.

essays.q: An adult animal produces young of its own kind. Which life process is shown? Give a scientific reason for your answer.
essays.answer: Reproduction. New individuals continue the group over generations. Not every individual must reproduce to be alive.

essays.q: Compare the birth of a kid with the hatching of a chick.
essays.answer: Goats normally give birth to live young and feed them milk. Different animal groups have different reproductive patterns.

essays.q: Explain the meaning of “Tendril”, including a supporting scientific point.
essays.answer: A slender plant structure that can coil around a support. Coiling helps attachment and support. The structure is not a root absorbing water from soil.

essays.q: A class compares plants that stand upright, climb or spread on the ground. Which feature are they comparing? Give a scientific reason for your answer.
essays.answer: Growth habit. Growth habit combines stem arrangement and support. Plant identification is stronger when observations are recorded before assigning labels.

essays.q: Explain the role of the stake in the bean vine’s growth.
essays.answer: The stem uses the stake for support rather than holding itself fully upright. Twining or tendrils may help attachment.

mcq.q: A seedling becomes taller and develops more leaves over two weeks. Which life process is shown?
mcq.method: Repeated measurements of the same plant support the conclusion. A brief change in water content alone is not enough to demonstrate lasting growth.

mcq.q: A viable dry seed later germinates after receiving suitable conditions. What earlier state explains its inactivity?
mcq.method: The embryo remained alive but relatively inactive. A failure to grow immediately does not prove that the seed is dead.

mcq.q: A plastic folder bends slightly without snapping. Which useful property is shown?
mcq.method: Flexibility concerns bending. A material can be flexible but not stretch very much, so flexibility and elasticity should not be confused.

mcq.q: Paper is cut into small pieces while remaining paper. Which general kind of change is shown?
wrong: Automatic formation of a new element
mcq.method: Cutting changes size and shape without making the material a new substance. It may still be difficult to restore the original sheet, showing that reversibility and chemical identity are different questions.
options: Automatic formation of a new element

mcq.q: Sand remains as grains after stirring in water. Which description applies?
mcq.method: The visible solid can settle or be trapped by a suitable filter. Its behaviour differs from dissolved salt in the same liquid.

mcq.q: In which direction does Earth generally rotate?
mcq.method: This rotation makes the Sun appear to move across the sky in the opposite broad direction. Appearance from the ground differs from the underlying cause.

mcq.q: The chest rises and falls as air moves in and out. Which process can be observed?
mcq.method: Breathing exchanges air. Cellular respiration releases energy chemically; breathing supports it by supplying oxygen and removing carbon dioxide.

mcq.q: A formerly living animal has died and no longer carries out life processes. Which category applies?
mcq.method: Its history includes life, unlike a rock. Temporary stillness or sleep does not by itself show death.

mcq.q: A clear plastic window lets a learner see a picture behind it. Which property is shown?
mcq.method: Light passes through so the image remains visible. Being colourless and being transparent are related observations but not the same definition.

mcq.q: Wood burns to ash and gases. Which process is shown?
mcq.method: Ash and gases differ from the starting wood. Cooling the products does not rebuild the original wood.

mcq.q: Sand and water are placed together without forming a new pure compound. What is made?
mcq.method: Components can often be separated by physical properties. Their proportions can vary without becoming one fixed-composition pure substance.

mcq.q: The Ghana mark turns to the side away from the torch. What is represented?
mcq.method: Earth blocks direct sunlight from reaching that side. The Sun continues producing light even though the location faces away.

mcq.q: Which organs form urine rather than merely storing it?
mcq.method: Kidneys form urine, whereas the bladder stores it before release. Both contribute to the urinary system but perform different jobs.

mcq.q: A bean plant produces viable seeds capable of making new bean plants. Which life process is represented?
mcq.method: New organisms arise through biological processes. A machine producing similar-looking objects is not evidence that the machine is alive.

mcq.q: A polished spoon feels even compared with coarse sandpaper. Which property describes the spoon’s surface?
mcq.method: Texture describes the surface rather than the entire object’s shape. Safe touching can compare texture without scratching or damaging samples.

essays.q: Explain the meaning of “Respiration”, including a supporting scientific point.
essays.answer: Chemical processes in cells that release usable energy from food. Cells require energy for movement, growth and repair, even when the person is not visibly active. Respiration is not simply moving air in and out.

essays.q: A plant shoot bends towards a light source. What is the bending in general biological terms? Give a scientific reason for your answer.
essays.answer: Response. The direction of light is the stimulus and bending growth is the response. Plants can respond slowly without walking.

essays.q: Give one difference and one connection between breathing and respiration.
essays.answer: Breathing exchanges air. Cellular respiration releases energy chemically; breathing supports it by supplying oxygen and removing carbon dioxide.

essays.q: Explain the meaning of “Artificial movement”, including a supporting scientific point.
essays.answer: Motion produced by a mechanism rather than evidence of an organism’s life processes. A motor moves the toy. It does not thereby reproduce biologically, obtain nutrients as an organism or grow through cellular processes.

essays.q: A learner uses growth records and a successful germination test to justify a classification. What supports the claim? Give a scientific reason for your answer.
essays.answer: Evidence. Recorded observations support the explanation. Where evidence is incomplete, the learner should acknowledge uncertainty rather than invent a result.

essays.q: Explain why a sleeping animal should not be classified this way merely because it is still.
essays.answer: Its history includes life, unlike a rock. Temporary stillness or sleep does not by itself show death.

essays.q: Explain the meaning of “Waterproof”, including a supporting scientific point.
essays.answer: Resistant to water passing through under the intended conditions. The coating or material resists water penetration. Seams and tears can still allow leaks, so the whole object must be checked.

essays.q: A cushion compresses readily when pressed. Which property is useful here? Give a scientific reason for your answer.
essays.answer: Softness. A soft filling changes shape under pressure and provides comfort. The outer cover may need different properties such as strength.

essays.q: Explain why transparency is useful for a viewing window.
essays.answer: Light passes through so the image remains visible. Being colourless and being transparent are related observations but not the same definition.

essays.q: Explain the meaning of “Irreversible change”, including a supporting scientific point.
essays.answer: A change not readily undone to restore the original under ordinary conditions. Cooking changes the egg’s materials in ways not reversed by cooling. The conclusion concerns ordinary practical reversal, not merely a change in temperature.

essays.q: Water slowly leaves a salt solution exposed to dry air. Which process removes the water? Give a scientific reason for your answer.
essays.answer: Evaporation. Water enters the air as vapour while dissolved salt may remain. Evaporation is not the same as destroying the water substance.

essays.q: Explain why burning wood is not reversed simply by cooling the ash.
essays.answer: Ash and gases differ from the starting wood. Cooling the products does not rebuild the original wood.

essays.q: Explain the meaning of “Residue”, including a supporting scientific point.
essays.answer: Material retained on a filter during filtration. It is the retained portion, not the liquid collected below. Naming both portions makes the method and result clear.

essays.q: Clearer liquid is gently poured away from settled sand. Which method is attempted? Give a scientific reason for your answer.
essays.answer: Decantation. The method works best after settling and with careful pouring. Fine suspended material can still remain in the poured liquid.

essays.q: Explain why sand and water are treated as a mixture.
essays.answer: Components can often be separated by physical properties. Their proportions can vary without becoming one fixed-composition pure substance.

essays.q: Explain the meaning of “Sunset”, including a supporting scientific point.
essays.answer: The apparent disappearance of the Sun below the local horizon as Earth turns. The observer’s view changes because Earth turns. The Sun continues lighting other parts of Earth.

essays.q: Which motion chiefly causes the regular alternation of day and night? Give a scientific reason for your answer.
essays.answer: Rotation. Turning changes which side faces sunlight. The yearly journey around the Sun is a different motion.

essays.q: Explain why night does not mean the Sun has switched off.
essays.answer: Earth blocks direct sunlight from reaching that side. The Sun continues producing light even though the location faces away.

essays.q: Explain the meaning of “Growth”, including a supporting scientific point.
essays.answer: A lasting increase in an organism’s size and usually its dry mass. Repeated measurements of the same plant support the conclusion. A brief change in water content alone is not enough to demonstrate lasting growth.

essays.q: The lungs remove carbon dioxide produced by cells. Which life process is this? Give a scientific reason for your answer.
essays.answer: Excretion. Carbon dioxide is a metabolic waste produced during aerobic respiration. Removing it is excretion, unlike removing undigested food by egestion.

essays.q: Distinguish the roles of the kidneys and bladder.
essays.answer: Kidneys form urine, whereas the bladder stores it before release. Both contribute to the urinary system but perform different jobs.

essays.q: Explain the meaning of “Dormancy”, including a supporting scientific point.
essays.answer: A low-activity state in which a viable organism can resume growth under suitable conditions. The embryo remained alive but relatively inactive. A failure to grow immediately does not prove that the seed is dead.

essays.q: Which continuing process supports a resting living animal even when it is not walking? Give a scientific reason for your answer.
essays.answer: Respiration. Living cells require energy for maintenance. Respiration is chemical activity in cells, not merely visible movement or breathing motions.

essays.q: Compare biological reproduction with a photocopier producing copies.
essays.answer: New organisms arise through biological processes. A machine producing similar-looking objects is not evidence that the machine is alive.

essays.q: Explain the meaning of “Flexible”, including a supporting scientific point.
essays.answer: Able to bend without readily breaking under suitable conditions. Flexibility concerns bending. A material can be flexible but not stretch very much, so flexibility and elasticity should not be confused.

essays.q: A learner chooses absorbent cloth for a towel instead of a plastic sheet. What process is being carried out? Give a scientific reason for your answer.
essays.answer: Material selection. The intended use determines which properties matter. No single material is best for every purpose.

essays.q: Distinguish surface texture from an object’s overall shape.
essays.answer: Texture describes the surface rather than the entire object’s shape. Safe touching can compare texture without scratching or damaging samples.

essays.q: Explain the meaning of “Physical change”, including a supporting scientific point.
essays.answer: A change such as shape or state without necessarily creating a new substance. Cutting changes size and shape without making the material a new substance. It may still be difficult to restore the original sheet, showing that reversibility and chemical identity are different questions.

essays.q: An ice cube becomes liquid water in a warm room. Which change occurs? Give a scientific reason for your answer.
essays.answer: Melting. Energy transfer changes the arrangement and movement of particles. Water is not lost merely because its solid shape disappears.

essays.q: Explain how this process relates to evaporation.
essays.answer: Cooling can return vapour to liquid. The water in the droplets was previously in gaseous form.

essays.q: Explain the meaning of “Insoluble”, including a supporting scientific point.
essays.answer: Not dissolving appreciably in a stated solvent under the conditions. The visible solid can settle or be trapped by a suitable filter. Its behaviour differs from dissolved salt in the same liquid.

essays.q: What is the liquid collected below the filter paper called? Give a scientific reason for your answer.
essays.answer: Filtrate. Passing through a filter does not prove drinking-water safety. Dissolved pollutants and some microbes may remain.

essays.q: Explain why stirring alone cannot permanently make the two liquids uniform.
essays.answer: A visible boundary enables separation of suitable liquid layers. Shaking may disperse droplets temporarily without making a permanent solution.

essays.q: Explain the meaning of “West to east”, including a supporting scientific point.
essays.answer: The direction of Earth’s rotation when described geographically. This rotation makes the Sun appear to move across the sky in the opposite broad direction. Appearance from the ground differs from the underlying cause.

essays.q: A ball with a marked location is used beside a lamp. What kind of teaching aid is this? Give a scientific reason for your answer.
essays.answer: Globe model. The model helps explain relationships but is not to scale in distance, size or speed. Model limits should be stated rather than hidden.

essays.q: Explain what the globe’s support represents and what it does not literally show.
essays.answer: The line runs between the poles in the model. It is not a physical stick running through real Earth for people to see.

essays.q: Explain the meaning of “Breathing”, including a supporting scientific point.
essays.answer: Movement of air into and out of the lungs. Breathing exchanges air. Cellular respiration releases energy chemically; breathing supports it by supplying oxygen and removing carbon dioxide.

essays.q: A person withdraws a hand from an uncomfortably hot surface. Which life process is shown? Give a scientific reason for your answer.
essays.answer: Sensitivity. Heat is the stimulus and withdrawing the hand is the response. The response protects the person from injury.

essays.q: Distinguish the stimulus from the response in the bright-light example.
essays.answer: The light is the change detected. Narrowing the eyes is the response, not the stimulus.

essays.q: Explain the meaning of “Dead organism”, including a supporting scientific point.
essays.answer: An organism that once lived but has irreversibly stopped its life processes. Its history includes life, unlike a rock. Temporary stillness or sleep does not by itself show death.

essays.q: A dry wooden plank was once part of a living tree. Which description fits its origin and present status? Give a scientific reason for your answer.
essays.answer: Dead plant material. The plank has a biological origin but does not carry out the life processes of a whole tree. A manufactured object can contain once-living material.

essays.q: Explain how a plant can respond without moving from place to place.
essays.answer: The plant responds through differential growth rather than walking. A slow response still provides evidence relevant to life.

essays.q: Explain the meaning of “Transparent”, including a supporting scientific point.
essays.answer: Allowing enough light through for objects to be seen clearly. Light passes through so the image remains visible. Being colourless and being transparent are related observations but not the same definition.

essays.q: A cloth towel takes up spilled water. Which property is useful? Give a scientific reason for your answer.
essays.answer: Absorbent. Water enters spaces in the fibres. A waterproof surface instead resists water passing through it.

essays.q: Explain why a hard material is not necessarily unbreakable.
essays.answer: Hardness concerns resistance to local deformation. A hard material may still fracture under impact; glass provides a familiar example.

mcq.q: A battery-powered toy car moves across the floor. What best describes this movement?
mcq.method: A motor moves the toy. It does not thereby reproduce biologically, obtain nutrients as an organism or grow through cellular processes.

mcq.q: A raincoat keeps rain from soaking clothing underneath. Which property is required?
mcq.method: The coating or material resists water penetration. Seams and tears can still allow leaks, so the whole object must be checked.

mcq.q: A cooked egg cannot simply be cooled back into a raw egg. Which description is appropriate?
