mcq.q: What is the sand left on the filter paper called?
mcq.method: It is the retained portion, not the liquid collected below. Naming both portions makes the method and result clear.

mcq.q: A location rotates away from the illuminated side and the Sun leaves view. What event is modelled?
mcq.method: The observer’s view changes because Earth turns. The Sun continues lighting other parts of Earth.

mcq.q: What is the original energy source driving many natural processes on Earth?
wrong: Energy made by the Moon’s light production
mcq.method: Solar radiation supplies light and contributes warming. It supports many processes but is not the only possible energy source anywhere on Earth.
options: Energy made by the Moon’s light production

mcq.q: Moist air rises and its temperature decreases. Which change can promote cloud formation?
mcq.method: Cooling can bring air to conditions where vapour condenses on suitable particles. Merely rising does not guarantee a cloud without sufficient moisture and suitable conditions.

mcq.q: Which dangerous gas may be produced by incompletely burning fuel and must not be confused with carbon dioxide?
mcq.method: The two names refer to different substances. Burning fuel in poorly ventilated spaces can expose people to carbon monoxide, requiring prevention rather than classroom experimentation.

mcq.q: Families, schools and local authorities cooperate to protect a water source. Which idea is illustrated?
mcq.method: Shared sources can be affected by many users. Cooperation, reporting hazards and safe routines protect people beyond one household.

mcq.q: Through which structures can carbon dioxide enter many leaves?
mcq.method: Gas exchange supports photosynthesis and respiration. Openings also allow water loss, so regulation is important.

mcq.q: Which part of the embryo develops into the young shoot in both plants?
mcq.method: The shoot eventually supports photosynthetic leaves. Its emergence is distinct from the initial root’s role.

mcq.q: The chest rises and falls as air moves in and out. Which process can be observed?
mcq.method: Breathing exchanges air. Cellular respiration releases energy chemically; breathing supports it by supplying oxygen and removing carbon dioxide.

mcq.q: A formerly living animal has died and no longer carries out life processes. Which category applies?
mcq.method: Its history includes life, unlike a rock. Temporary stillness or sleep does not by itself show death.

mcq.q: A clear plastic window lets a learner see a picture behind it. Which property is shown?
mcq.method: Light passes through so the image remains visible. Being colourless and being transparent are related observations but not the same definition.

essays.q: Explain the meaning of “Stimulus”, including a supporting scientific point.
essays.answer: A detectable change that can trigger a response. The light is the change detected. Narrowing the eyes is the response, not the stimulus.

essays.q: Which respiratory waste gas moves from the blood into the lungs to be breathed out? Give a scientific reason for your answer.
essays.answer: Carbon dioxide. Cells produce carbon dioxide; blood carries it to the lungs and breathing removes it. Oxygen is taken in for aerobic respiration rather than being its waste gas.

essays.q: Describe how you would collect evidence that a seedling is growing.
essays.answer: Repeated measurements of the same plant support the conclusion. A brief change in water content alone is not enough to demonstrate lasting growth.

essays.q: Explain the meaning of “Response to stimuli”, including a supporting scientific point.
essays.answer: A change in activity caused by detecting an environmental change. The plant responds through differential growth rather than walking. A slow response still provides evidence relevant to life.

essays.q: A healthy seedling grows and responds to light. Which category fits it? Give a scientific reason for your answer.
essays.answer: Living thing. Growth and response support the classification, while respiration also occurs. Several life-process observations provide stronger evidence than one superficial feature.

essays.q: Explain why a dry seed needs a viability test rather than classification by appearance alone.
essays.answer: The embryo remained alive but relatively inactive. A failure to grow immediately does not prove that the seed is dead.

essays.q: Explain the meaning of “Hardness”, including a supporting scientific point.
essays.answer: Resistance of a material to indentation or scratching. Hardness concerns resistance to local deformation. A hard material may still fracture under impact; glass provides a familiar example.

essays.q: Sandpaper helps remove small surface layers because of which texture? Give a scientific reason for your answer.
essays.answer: Rough texture. A rough surface can rub against and abrade another material. The same property can be unsuitable for something meant to feel gentle on skin.

essays.q: Distinguish bending from stretching using a familiar example.
essays.answer: Flexibility concerns bending. A material can be flexible but not stretch very much, so flexibility and elasticity should not be confused.

essays.q: Explain the meaning of “Freezing”, including a supporting scientific point.
essays.answer: A change from liquid to solid. Removing enough thermal energy permits solid formation. It is the reverse state change of melting.

essays.q: Salt grains become invisible when stirred into water. Which process occurs? Give a scientific reason for your answer.
essays.answer: Dissolving. The salt remains distributed through the solution and can be recovered by suitable water removal. It has not disappeared from existence.

essays.q: Explain why an irreversible-looking change need not always be chemical.
essays.answer: Cutting changes size and shape without making the material a new substance. It may still be difficult to restore the original sheet, showing that reversibility and chemical identity are different questions.

essays.q: Explain the meaning of “Evaporation”, including a supporting scientific point.
essays.answer: Conversion of liquid to vapour, usable for recovering a non-volatile dissolved solid. The solvent is removed, leaving the salt. This simple method does not collect the water unless vapour is also captured and condensed.

essays.q: A teacher drains the lower layer and closes a tap near the oil–water boundary. Which apparatus is used? Give a scientific reason for your answer.
essays.answer: Separating funnel. The lower layer exits first, so the boundary is watched carefully. Fully miscible liquids do not provide that separable boundary.

essays.q: Compare the separation of sand from water with removal of dissolved salt.
essays.answer: The visible solid can settle or be trapped by a suitable filter. Its behaviour differs from dissolved salt in the same liquid.

essays.q: Explain the meaning of “Simultaneous day and night”, including a supporting scientific point.
essays.answer: The occurrence of daylight in one part of Earth while another faces away from the Sun. Only the side facing the source receives direct light. Locations on opposite sides can therefore experience different times of day.

essays.q: The Ghana mark on a globe faces the torch. Which condition is represented? Give a scientific reason for your answer.
essays.answer: Daylight. The lamp-facing side receives light. A full classroom room may still have stray light, so the model simplifies real conditions.

essays.q: Relate Earth’s turning to the Sun’s apparent daily movement.
essays.answer: This rotation makes the Sun appear to move across the sky in the opposite broad direction. Appearance from the ground differs from the underlying cause.

essays.q: Explain the meaning of “Food chain”, including a supporting scientific point.
essays.answer: A sequence showing transfer of food matter and energy between organisms. Energy stored by the producer passes through feeding relationships. Organisms do not pass all received energy unchanged to the next level.

essays.q: The Sun helps water leave the sea, later forming clouds and rain. Which larger cycle is supported? Give a scientific reason for your answer.
essays.answer: Water cycle. Solar energy supports evaporation and the return of water to the atmosphere. Gravity and other conditions help later movements such as rainfall and runoff.

essays.q: Explain how sunlight helps us see objects without looking at the Sun.
essays.answer: Light reaches objects and some is reflected to the eyes. Visibility is different from staring directly at the source, which is unsafe for the Sun.

essays.q: Explain the meaning of “Condensation nuclei”, including a supporting scientific point.
essays.answer: Small airborne particles on which water can begin condensing. Water condenses onto small surfaces. This does not mean every visible cloud is simply dust without water.

essays.q: Rainwater soaks into a garden rather than immediately running away. Which process occurs? Give a scientific reason for your answer.
essays.answer: Infiltration. Soil spaces receive water that may later be stored or move deeper. Surface condition and soil properties affect the rate.

essays.q: Distinguish humid air from a visible cloud.
essays.answer: The gas is usually invisible. Visible mist and clouds contain small droplets or ice rather than being a direct view of the invisible gas.

essays.q: Explain the meaning of “Carbon storage”, including a supporting scientific point.
essays.answer: Retention of carbon in materials such as growing plants and soil. Some carbon remains in biomass for a period. It can return through respiration, decay or burning, so storage is part of a cycle rather than permanent disappearance.

essays.q: Which process removes carbon dioxide from the air while green plants make food in suitable conditions? Give a scientific reason for your answer.
essays.answer: Photosynthesis. Carbon becomes part of plant material. Plants also respire, so their gas exchanges depend on the processes occurring rather than one simple rule for every moment.

essays.q: Distinguish a useful natural effect from problems caused by increasing its strength.
essays.answer: A natural greenhouse effect helps keep Earth warmer than it would otherwise be. Increasing greenhouse-gas concentrations can enhance warming and disrupt climate.

essays.q: Explain the meaning of “Sewage”, including a supporting scientific point.
essays.answer: Wastewater that may contain human waste and disease-causing organisms. Human-waste contamination can transmit disease. Treatment and sanitation should prevent it reaching drinking-water sources.

essays.q: Smoke from open waste burning enters a classroom. Which environmental problem occurs? Give a scientific reason for your answer.
essays.answer: Air pollution. Smoke can contain harmful particles and gases. Avoiding unnecessary burning reduces exposure rather than relying on people to tolerate it.

essays.q: Explain why pupils should not collect unknown chemical waste during a clean-up.
essays.answer: Keeping waste out of drains reduces blockages and movement into water. Hazardous materials need specialised handling beyond ordinary litter collection.

essays.q: Explain the meaning of “Branching roots”, including a supporting scientific point.
essays.answer: A spreading root arrangement reaching more soil and providing anchorage. A wider spread explores more soil and supports the plant. The arrangement still needs suitable water and oxygen conditions to function well.

essays.q: Which tissue moves food made in leaves toward growing or storage parts? Give a scientific reason for your answer.
essays.answer: Phloem. Sugar can move from producing regions to places needing or storing it. This differs from the principal water-and-mineral role of xylem.

essays.q: Explain how a broad leaf surface can support photosynthesis.
essays.answer: A broad surface can intercept light, although leaf shapes vary with species and conditions. Surface area is one adaptation, not a universal identical design.

essays.q: Explain the meaning of “Epigeal germination”, including a supporting scientific point.
essays.answer: A pattern in which cotyledons are carried above the ground during emergence. Elongation below the cotyledons lifts them in this example. The pattern should be confirmed by observations rather than assumed for every plant called a bean.

essays.q: What is the general name for each of the two fleshy seed leaves in a common bean? Give a scientific reason for your answer.
essays.answer: Cotyledon. Common bean has two cotyledons, which hold important food reserves. Maize has one cotyledon with a different role in obtaining stored food.

essays.q: Compare the main reserve locations in these two seeds.
essays.answer: Maize retains substantial reserves in endosperm, while common bean stores much in cotyledons. Both use reserves before photosynthesis supplies enough food.
